SSTGAM in 3D: one surface over value and time

Synthetic data with a known effect: 4,000 patients, one lab measured daily for 15 days, about 25% of days missing. Every surface plots lab value x day x contribution to the log-odds, centred so 0 is an average observation. Spline penalty chosen by "auto": 0.104.

One surface over value and time

Each lab gets a single effect surface over (value, day), learned from all days at once. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, hover for values. The true effect is monotone early and U-shaped late; both models recover that change over time, the spline as a smooth surface, the tree as a table of value bins by day.

Why sharing across time matters

The first two treat each day as an unrelated feature, so day 7 learns nothing from days 6 and 8: the same spline GAM fitted per day, and EBM (interactions=0), which fits one boosted shape function per column. Their 15 curves come out noisy and jump from day to day. SSTGAM pools every day into one surface, so neighbouring days inform each other. Shape error is the RMS gap to the true effect over the observed training cells (lower is better); all four are centred per day, the only level a per-day model can identify.

Spline training: penalized Newton steps on the whole surface

Each Newton step updates every coefficient of the surface at once, across all days. Press Play or drag the slider: the full value x time shape appears within two steps; later steps only polish it. Iteration 0 is the base-rate model (a flat surface).

Tree training: hundreds of small boosting updates

Each round fits a shallow tree to the current residual statistics of the whole value-bin x day table and adds a damped step. The surface builds up gradually: coarse value splits first, then splits along time, then refinements.

Scoring one patient: the trajectory reads the surface day by day

The grey path on the floor of each box is one patient's lab over 15 days; it breaks on the 5 missing days. Each observed day looks up the model at (value, day); the coloured stems rise or fall from 0 by what that day adds to the log-odds. In SSTGAM missing days add nothing; EBM learns a separate score for a missing value on each day, shown in its panel title. The same low value lowers risk early and raises it late.
